unmapped_findings: Measured composition of Fe-7Al-0.35C (Table IV): Al 6.78, Si 0.19, Mn 0.15, S 0.004, C 0.35 wt.% [b0052].
The volume fraction of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates increases significantly with increasing carbon content [b0061].
The increase in bulk hardness with increasing carbon (Table V) suggests precipitation hardening by hard Fe3AlC0.5 is the predominant strengthening mechanism in these alloys [b0062].

The addition of carbon to Fe-7 wt.% Al alloy resulted in significant improvement in room-temperature strength (396–610 MPa), while room-temperature tensile elongation decreases significantly (18–3%) with increasing carbon content [b0062].

Fe-7 wt.% Al alloys are not susceptible to environmental embrittlement; the decrease in room-temperature ductility with increasing carbon is attributed solely to the increase in volume fraction of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates [b0062].

Table V and Fig. 5 captions label the carbon-series route 'AIM', whereas the section text (b0060) states the alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC) [b0053,b0055,b0060].
